subject: Operational availability baseline + burst exemption — template edits
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@horizondw.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Operational availability ask during Nov migration

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team is excited. We have one operational ask from procurement/security as we move to a pilot in November: during our data migration window (Nov 20-27) we expect burst traffic that could temporarily push our p95 above the standard latency SLO. Procurement is asking for a narrow, time-boxed carveout in the SLA template so we don't trigger monthly credits for predictable migration-induced load.

Specifically: can Redwood add a "migration exception" clause that allows a single contiguous 7-day window per year where availability and latency remedies are adjusted (i.e., a higher latency threshold and no monthly credit for known migration activity), provided Horizon gives 10 business days' notice and submits a migration runbook?

We'd like to lock the pilot term this week — can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with (a) an exception clause with the notice/runbook requirement and (b) how monthly credits would be handled for that window? Attached is our preliminary runbook and historical traffic for your reference.

Best,
Maya Thompson
Head of Cloud Operations
Horizon DataWorks

Attachment: hdw-nov-migration-runbook.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: hdw-nov-traffic-snapshot.csv (csv)

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T17:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability ask during Nov migration

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear note and the runbook.

Short answer: we can include a migration exception clause, but we need to define the operational guardrails so the exception isn't abused. Proposed high-level terms from my side:
- One contiguous window per 12-month period, up to 7 days.
- Customer must provide 10 business days' advance notice and a migration runbook; Redwood must acknowledge receipt.
- During the window: latency SLOs are relaxed to p95 = baseline + 2x (but availability floor remains — see below).
- No automatic monthly service credit for resilience deviations that are directly attributable to the documented migration activity. Any other failures remain creditable.
- Redwood reserves the right to suspend exception if there is evidence of misconfiguration or pattern of repeated abuse.

Laura / Ben — looping you in to help turn this into a short contract-ready paragraph and to quantify how credits would be reported in the monthly statement when a migration exception is in effect. I attached our current SLA draft (redwood-sla-draft-v3.docx) with a placeholder clause.

Maya — can you confirm the migration runbook delivery date and whether your infra team will provide an on-call contact for the window?

Thanks,
Sergio
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-v3.docx (docx)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:11:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability ask during Nov migration

Thanks Sergio / Maya — drafted a short paragraph below that we can insert into the template (see bolded text for the clause). Ben, please confirm the credit-report mechanics.

--- DRAFT CLAUSE (for insertion into Section 4: Remedies) ---
Migration Exception: Customer may request a single, contiguous migration exception window not to exceed seven (7) consecutive calendar days in any 12‑month period ("Migration Window"). To be eligible, Customer must provide Redwood with at least ten (10) business days' prior written notice and a migration runbook that describes the expected traffic profile, mitigation plans, and an on-call contact. During an approved Migration Window, Redwood will: (i) apply a temporary relaxation to latency commitments limited to p95 latency = baseline p95 * 2.0 for the Migration Window only; and (ii) exclude deviations directly and solely caused by the documented migration activity from calculation of monthly service credits. All other availability and reliability obligations remain in effect. Redwood reserves the right to decline or terminate a Migration Window if the runbook or observed activity indicates elevated operational risk.
--- end draft ---

Ben — for monthly statements we propose: include an appendix line that marks the Migration Window dates and exclude any metric periods fully contained within the window from credit calculations. Partially overlapping metric periods should be prorated; if you prefer a different approach (e.g., pro-rata credits or a fixed waiver), propose it here.

Maya — if this aligns, we'll send a redlined doc with the clause inserted and a short addendum that lists the notice/runbook requirements.

- Laura
VP, Legal & Contracts (Redwood Inference)

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-v3-redline.docx (docx)

From: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@horizondw.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability ask during Nov migration

Laura / Sergio — this looks reasonable and thank you for the pragmatic approach. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
1) The p95 * 2.0 relaxation is fine, but could you confirm whether that applies to both regional and global p95 reporting? Our pilot will use both US and EU regions and we need the same treatment in both dashboards.
2) For partially overlapping metric windows, Horizon prefers a prorated approach (exclude hours fully in the Migration Window; prorate mixed windows).
3) We'll deliver the runbook by EOD 2026-11-15 and our infra on-call will be maya.oncall@horizondw.com.

We also attached our metric snapshot — please verify you have the same baselines on your side.

Regards,
Maya

Attachment: hdw-nov-traffic-snapshot.csv (csv)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Operational availability ask during Nov migration

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 11:03 AM Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@horizondw.com> wrote:
> Laura / Sergio — this looks reasonable and thank you for the pragmatic approach. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
> 1) The p95 * 2.0 relaxation is fine, but could you confirm whether that applies to both regional and global p95 reporting?
> 2) For partially overlapping metric windows, Horizon prefers a prorated approach (exclude hours fully in the Migration Window; prorate mixed windows).

Hi Maya — quick answers:
1) We'll apply the relaxation to any metric scope the customer uses to measure latency in the contract (region-specific or global) — we'll mark the scope in the Migration Window acknowledgement. In short: yes, we can mirror region-level or account-level metrics as requested and will reflect that in the addendum.
2) Agreed on the prorated approach; we'll define the prorating rule in the addendum (hours fully in window excluded; mixed hours prorated by minute).

Next steps: Laura will circulate a redlined SLA with the Migration Exception paragraph inserted and an addendum that specifies metric scope and prorating rules. Maya — once we have your runbook (EOD 11/15) we'll acknowledge the Migration Window and add the dates to the contract appendix.

Ben Carter
Principal, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: system-uptime-metrics.csv (internal)
